paragraphs.text: A loose [Liu Bao](liu-bao:definition) from Guangxi, made in 1960 and now sixty-six years old. The trade counts a Liu Bao as [aged](liu-bao:age-aged) after about ten years, so this one passed that point more than five decades ago.

Like every [dark tea](dark:definition), its leaf was piled after it was made, so that warmth, moisture and microbes could slowly change it, and then it was packed away to age. Tea this old is hard to date. The trade reads its age from the basket, the labels and the papers packed with it, and much of it is [old stock](liu-bao:old-stock).

brewing.text: Liu Bao takes very hot or boiling water, because its leaf is dense and gives up its depth slowly. Rinse it once or twice and pour the rinse away. Use about 5 to 8 grams to 100 ml, start with steeps of five to fifteen seconds and add a few seconds each round; a good Liu Bao gives ten cups or more.

notice.text: A deep red, thick cup with woody, herbal and betel nut notes; tea several decades old is often described with ginseng and camphor.
